summary_html: Agency fails to **disclose required data or reports**, obstructing transparency. Federal statutes require public reporting under CAPTA, FOIA, and Sunshine provisions.
authority_html:
- **CAPTA (42 U.S.C. §§ 5101–5116)** — mandates public availability of child-fatality information  
- **Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. § 552)** — public access to federal records  
- **Government in the Sunshine Act (5 U.S.C. § 552b)** — open-meeting requirements

primary_citations.citation_text: Montana - Title 41, Chapter 3 (Child Abuse and Neglect – mandatory reporting and protective services)

regulations_applicable.title: Department 37 - PUBLIC HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: Mercer v. Montana Department of Public Health & Human Services
key_cases.holding: A mandatory preliminary injunction requiring DPHHS to disclose child abuse and neglect case records to a state legislator conducting a statutory review under § 41-3-205(4) was affirmed; the legislator had an absolute statutory right to the described records subject only to the statute's own limits, and a stipulation barring further disclosure minimized any harm to the Department.
key_cases.relevance: It is the controlling Montana decision rejecting an agency's attempt to narrow a statutory disclosure obligation for child-protection records.
key_cases.quote: This statute requires that child abuse and neglect “case records” be kept confidential but also provides for disclosure of such records upon satisfaction of statutory criteria

key_cases.holding: Any Montana citizen has standing under Article II, Section 9 to seek judicial relief for a denial of access to the documents of any Montana public body, without needing a nexus to or residence in that body's jurisdiction; the individual-privacy limitation and any confidentiality provisions remain to be applied on remand.
key_cases.relevance: It is the Montana Supreme Court's standing rule for suing over a refusal to disclose public records, subject to the individual-privacy balance.
key_cases.quote: We hold Article II, Section 9 grants a right to judicial relief to a Montana citizen alleging denial of access to a document of a Montana public body.

key_cases.case_name: In re Petition of Missoula County Public Schools
key_cases.holding: The district court's in camera, document-by-document balancing of individual privacy against the merits of public disclosure was affirmed; investigatory documents in a public employee's personnel file were not protected where the employee occupied a position of public trust.
key_cases.relevance: It forecloses the common agency response that investigatory or personnel records are categorically exempt, and requires a fact-specific privacy balance instead.
key_cases.quote: There is no blanket exemption from the right to know for documents simply because they are contained in a personnel file.

key_cases.case_name: Billings Gazette v. City of Billings
key_cases.holding: The order requiring the City to disclose the identities of five employees disciplined for viewing pornography on City computers was reversed: under the three-step Article II, Section 9 analysis, a public employee who holds no position of public trust and whose misconduct violated no duty requiring a high level of public trust has a reasonable expectation of privacy in his identity in internal disciplinary matters that clearly exceeds the merits of disclosure.
key_cases.relevance: It is Montana's controlling right-to-know privacy-balancing framework and the necessary caution to any transparency demand: the balance can and does come out against disclosure when the individual holds no position of public trust.
key_cases.quote: each request requires a fact specific, case-by-case analysis of the interests at issue and a balancing of the demands of individual privacy and the merits of public disclosure
